findings: Ownership of contract concepts is correct: dyn.contract.* are owned by the new contract entity type, and the contract entity type is declared in both proposal.entity_types and ontology.entity_types. No business-owned concept is used to carry a contract fact.

dyn.contract.value correctly carries a required currency qualifier sourced from contracts[0].value.currency and is defined as the maximum contract value over its life, not annual expenditure or business income. Validation shows 18/18 emitted with currency AUD; no income concept is reused.

dyn.contract.item_classification_code is correctly contract-owned and scheme-qualified (UNSPSC), and is explicitly not mapped to entity.industry_code / ext.entity.industry_code. This avoids the ANZSIC-vs-UNSPSC mislabel.
dyn.contract.status and dyn.contract.procurement_method are correctly contract-owned and do not reuse entity.status; the definitions state they are not the supplier's registration status.

entity.legal_name reuse for supplier and procuring_entity is a bounded approximation: the rationale states the publisher does not distinguish registered from trading names and no current_legal_name claim_scope is set. No legal form is inferred from 'LLC', 'P.C.', 'Limited' or 'The Trustee for ... Trust'.

entity.abn reuse is gated on scheme == AU-ABN and uses the abn checksum transform; validation shows 0 value errors on 16 supplier and 18 procuring-entity emissions. Absence of ABN is treated as abstention, not as evidence of no ABN.

address.state reuse for supplier coerces 'Outside Australia' to OTHER and the rationale explicitly bounds OTHER as 'not an Australian state/territory', not a location. Foreign postcodes ('96960', '22102-1036') are kept as written and not asserted to be Australian.

Supplier contactPoint.email and contactPoint.telephone are correctly unmapped: held-out rows show the buyer's boilerplate (procurement@niaa.gov.au / '02 6261 1111') on foreign suppliers, so mapping them to the supplier would be a wrong-entity claim. This is a correct abstention, not missing coverage.

procuring_entity_party.contactPoint.email is unmapped with an explicit reason (role_email transform drops tenders@finance.gov.au 18/18). This is a transform misclassification recorded as a finding, not an invented claim; the abstention is honest.

Amendment fields (contracts[0].amendments[0].id / releaseID / amendsReleaseID) are unmapped with reason 'not present in the inspected snapshot'. However, held-out row ordinal 19 (tag 'contractAmendment') DOES contain contracts[0].amendments[0].id = 'CN4280171-A1', releaseID and amendsReleaseID. The stated reason is therefore factually wrong for the held-out partition, and the contract key contracts[0].id = 'CN4280171' collides with the original release. This is a bounded identity limitation already disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number, but the unmapped reason text is inaccurate.

CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO and CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY edges emit 18/18 each. The rationale correctly states no equality guard is executed between awards[0].suppliers[0].id and the role-bound supplier party id, and that multiple supplier-role parties refuse the row. This is an honest bound, not a claimed guard.

observation.observed_at uses releases[].date with fallback resource_last_modified; the rationale correctly notes parse_date truncates time and that this is publication time, not valid_from or contract start. No invented local-midnight convention is claimed for start/end dates; the UTC-date truncation and possible ±1 day local divergence are explicitly bounded.
dyn.contract.limited_tender_exempt maps raw '1'->true and '0'->false with default 'unknown'; both true and false are observed (ordinals 15, 31). Blank is 'unknown', never false. Correct.

dyn.contract.limited_tender_reason_code and dyn.contract.limited_tender_reason are observed on one row only (ordinal 31, 'TR' and the 10.3.d.iii text) and the definitions state coverage is limited to that single observation. No over-claim of population coverage.

No duplicate concepts detected: dyn.contract.notice_number is distinct from observation.source_record_id (release id) and from entity.abn/acn; dyn.contract.signed_at / start_date / end_date are distinct from entity.date_registered, ext.entity.date_established and ext.licence.start_date/end_date.

No hidden index assumption is claimed: the config uses contracts[0], items[0], additionalIdentifiers[0] and awards[0] as singleton indexed collections, and the execution contract states multiple members refuse the row. The proposal does not claim silent first-item retention for repeated arrays.
semantic_risks: dyn.contract.notice_number key collides across original and amendment releases (held-out ordinal 19 shows tag 'contractAmendment' with the same contracts[0].id 'CN4280171' as the original). The engine appends observations rather than overwriting, so this is a bounded recall/identity limitation, but downstream consumers must not treat notice_number as a unique contract key.

entity.legal_name for suppliers is a published party name, not a registrar-stated legal name. Names like 'RMI Cleaning Services, LLC', 'MILES AND STOCKBRIDGE P.C.' and 'The Trustee for ... Trust' must not be read as legal-form evidence; the mapping states this but the concept name still invites over-reading.

address.state OTHER conflates all non-Australian regions and loses the raw text ('Outside Australia'). The raw region is not preserved anywhere; this is a bounded loss, not an incorrect claim, but downstream state-based filters will misclassify foreign suppliers as OTHER.

dyn.contract.start_date / end_date truncate a UTC timestamp whose time component varies (14:00Z vs 13:00Z), so the emitted date may differ from the local contract day by one. This is disclosed but remains a precision risk for term-length calculations.

Only contracts[0].items[0] is captured; additional items and additional contracts in a release are not expanded. This is a bounded coverage limitation, not an incorrect claim, but item-level completeness is not achieved.

awards[0].date is unmapped on the basis that it equals dateSigned in observed rows; held-out ordinal 19 shows awards[0].date = '2026-10-01T07:06:02Z' while the release date is '2026-10-21T05:28:07Z', so the award date is not a publication timestamp. The unmapped reason acknowledges this, but the equality-to-dateSigned claim is only true for non-amendment rows.
checked_reuse: entity.legal_name: reused for supplier and procuring_entity with bounded 'published party name' scope; no legal-form inference. Acceptable as bounded approximation.
entity.abn: reused with AU-ABN scheme gate and checksum transform; no legal-form inference. Correct.
address.locality / address.state / address.postcode / address.country: reused for the party's own stated address; foreign values kept as written; OTHER bounded. Correct ownership (business).
observation.source_record_id / observed_at / source_id / licence: reused with correct semantics (release id, publication date, dataset id, cc-by). Correct.

ext.contact.role_email / ext.contact.phone: proposed for procuring entity only, but both are unmapped in the final mapping due to transform misclassification / boilerplate. No wrong-entity contact claim emitted.
entity.status: NOT reused for contract status; dyn.contract.status is a separate contract-owned enum. Correct.
entity.industry_code / ext.entity.industry_code: NOT reused for UNSPSC item classification; dyn.contract.item_classification_code is contract-owned and scheme-qualified. Correct.
ext.financial.total_income / taxable_income / tax_payable / revenue_band: NOT reused for contract value; dyn.contract.value is contract-owned with currency qualifier. Correct.
ext.licence.start_date / end_date: NOT reused for contract term; dyn.contract.start_date / end_date are contract-owned. Correct.
ext.entity.date_established / entity.date_registered: NOT reused for contract signed_at. Correct.
critic.rationale: The mapping is semantically sound on ownership, units/currency, time scopes and role binding: contract facts are contract-owned, business facts are business-owned, contract value is currency-qualified and not income, UNSPSC is not ANZSIC, ABNs are checksum-gated, and supplier contact boilerplate is correctly abstained. The remaining blocking issue is a factual inaccuracy in the unmapped reasons for the amendment fields: the proposal states contracts[0].amendments[0].id / releaseID / amendsReleaseID are 'not present in the inspected snapshot', but held-out row ordinal 19 (tag 'contractAmendment') contains all three. The contract key collision this creates is already disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number, so the fix is to correct the unmapped reason text (and optionally note the observed amendment row) rather than to invent an amendment concept from a single held-out observation. All other risks are explicitly bounded (OTHER state conflation, UTC-date truncation, notice_number non-uniqueness, first-item-only capture, legal_name approximation) and are not known semantic errors. Verdict is revise for the inaccurate unmapped reason; no wrong-owner, invented scheme/currency, or unsupported legal-name claim was found.

blocking_findings.field: proposal.unmapped[contracts[0].amendments[0].id].reason (and mapping.unmapped same path; also amendments[0].releaseID and amendments[0].amendsReleaseID)
blocking_findings.actual: Reason states 'Amendment fields are not present in the inspected snapshot (no nonempty values in the column profile)' / 'Not present in the inspected snapshot'.
blocking_findings.expected: Reason should acknowledge that amendment fields ARE present on at least one held-out row (tag 'contractAmendment') and explain why they are still left unmapped (e.g. single observation, no amendment entity type, contract key collision already disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number).
blocking_findings.evidence: heldout_examples ordinal 19 row contains contracts[0].amendments[0].id = 'CN4280171-A1', contracts[0].amendments[0].releaseID = 'prod-2416a68113334cca9867238cb761658c-927300ea26db3e1e8fb91d355fbcc4fe', contracts[0].amendments[0].amendsReleaseID = 'prod-2416a68113334cca9867238cb761658c-8ea45a4cba6b302f9a4c4cc4babc2319', with tag 'contractAmendment' and contracts[0].id 'CN4280171'.
blocking_findings.correction: Replace the three amendment unmapped reasons with text that states the fields are observed on at least one amendment release (held-out ordinal 19) but are left unmapped because (a) only one observation exists, (b) there is no amendment entity type, and (c) the contract key contracts[0].id collides across original and amendment releases as already disclosed in dyn.contract.notice_number. Do not propose an amendment concept from a single held-out row.
